findings.title: DMARC not enforced (p=none): domain can be spoofed for BEC/wire fraud

evidence.excerpt: DMARC record: v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@brightwaterfleet.example; policy=none, pct=100, rua=true.

findings.deal_impact: Domain can be spoofed in phishing/BEC and wire-fraud attempts targeting customers and finance, creating fraud, incident-response and insurability risk until enforcement is enabled.

remediation.summary: Move DMARC from p=none through quarantine to reject after validating all legitimate senders and alignment.

findings.title: SPF uses soft/neutral fail

evidence.excerpt: TXT SPF record: v=spf1 include:_spf.mailhost.example include:sendgrid.example ~all; qualifier=~all, lookup_count=2.

findings.deal_impact: Soft-fail SPF weakens spoofing resistance and compounds the DMARC monitoring-only posture, increasing email impersonation risk.

remediation.summary: Audit authorized senders and change SPF qualifier from ~all to -all once legitimate sources are confirmed.

findings.title: DNSSEC not enabled

evidence.excerpt: DS record query result: enabled=false.

findings.deal_impact: Unsigned DNS leaves resolution more exposed to cache poisoning/redirection, a lower-likelihood but relevant trust and availability risk.

remediation.summary: Enable DNSSEC at the registrar/DNS provider, publish DS records, and monitor validation.

findings.title: Publicly logged hostnames suggest exposed admin/legacy/staging systems

evidence.excerpt: Risky hostname pattern=vpn; first_seen=2023-02-11, last_seen=2026-09-30.
Risky hostname pattern=jenkins|old; first_seen=2021-06-03, last_seen=2026-08-14.
Risky hostname pattern=staging; first_seen=2024-01-20, last_seen=2026-10-01.
Risky hostname pattern=legacy; first_seen=2019-11-05, last_seen=2026-07-22.

findings.deal_impact: Four publicly logged risky names suggest admin, VPN, staging and legacy attack surface that may be unmanaged; validate ownership, exposure and patching in diligence.

remediation.summary: Inventory the four risky hostnames, remove or isolate legacy/staging systems, restrict admin/VPN access, and confirm monitoring.

findings.title: Large certificate footprint relative to company size

evidence.excerpt: unique_hostnames=47; risky_hostnames_count=4.

findings.deal_impact: 47 unique hostnames for a 201-1000 employee company suggests asset sprawl that can weaken inventory, patching and decommissioning discipline.

remediation.summary: Reconcile all 47 CT hostnames to owners and business purpose; decommission orphaned services and maintain an external asset inventory.

findings.title: Deprecated TLS versions offered

evidence.excerpt: tls_support: TLSv1.0=true, TLSv1.1=true, TLSv1.2=true; tls_versions=[TLSv1.0, TLSv1.1, TLSv1.2].

findings.deal_impact: Deprecated TLS on www may expose sessions to known protocol weaknesses and complicate PCI/customer security reviews.

remediation.summary: Disable TLSv1.0 and TLSv1.1 on www, retain TLSv1.2+ only, and verify cipher configuration.

findings.title: HSTS not set

evidence.excerpt: Header strict-transport-security=null.
Header strict-transport-security=null.

findings.deal_impact: Without HSTS, users can be downgraded to insecure HTTP on first visit, increasing interception and session-hijack risk.

remediation.summary: Set Strict-Transport-Security on apex and www after confirming HTTPS coverage for all subdomains.

findings.title: Internet-facing appliance listed in CISA KEV (version not verified)

evidence.excerpt: Fingerprint product=ExampleGate SSL-VPN, version=7.0.11, kind=appliance, source=asset_path.

KEV match CVE-PLACEHOLDER-0001, vendor=ExampleGate, product=ExampleGate SSL-VPN, match_level=product, match_tier=appliance_exposed; note: KEV lists products, not affected versions; version not verified.

findings.deal_impact: Potential exposure: an internet-facing SSL-VPN product matches CISA KEV at product level only, so version/patch status must be urgently verified; if vulnerable, exploitation could drive deal and insurance risk.

remediation.summary: Immediately verify ExampleGate SSL-VPN 7.0.11 patch status against the KEV entry, patch or isolate the appliance, and review logs for compromise.

findings.title: Publicly disclosed security incident in the last 24 months

evidence.excerpt: State AG breach notice dated 2025-08-14: unauthorized access to a customer support system; approx. 3,100 individuals notified. disclosed_within_months=14; entity_match=exact.

findings.deal_impact: A disclosed incident 14 months ago raises questions on root cause, remediation, notification obligations, customer impact and insurability; obtain incident and regulator records in diligence.

remediation.summary: Request incident timeline, forensics summary, remediation evidence and lessons learned; verify all notifications and control fixes are closed.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in logical access controls (CC6.1)

evidence.excerpt: Exception noted. 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts were not enforced for MFA. These were service-desk accounts created via a legacy provisioning script that bypassed the conditional access policy.

findings.deal_impact: MFA exception - 4 sampled admin accounts were not enforced for MFA, indicating a control gap in enforcement that could lead to unauthorized access.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC6.1 exception: MFA is enforced for all administrative access to production systems.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in logical access controls (CC6.2)

evidence.excerpt: Exception noted. 3 of 15 terminated users retained active access for 6, 11, and 19 business days respectively.

findings.deal_impact: Access-review exception - 3 terminated users retained active access beyond the 1-business-day requirement.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC6.2 exception: Access for terminated employees is revoked within 1 business day of termination.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in security monitoring (CC7.2)

evidence.excerpt: Exception noted. For 2 consecutive weeks (Nov 10–23, 2025), alerts were forwarded to a decommissioned distribution list and were not reviewed.

findings.deal_impact: Significant exception - SIEM alerts were not reviewed for 2 consecutive weeks due to routing to a decommissioned distribution list.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC7.2 exception: Security alerts generated by the SIEM are reviewed and triaged daily.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in change management (CC8.1)

evidence.excerpt: Exception noted. 2 of 40 changes lacked documented approval (emergency hotfixes).

findings.deal_impact: Change-management exception - 2 sampled production changes lacked documented peer approval.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC8.1 exception: Production changes are approved by a peer before deployment.

findings.title: SOC 2 report period ended more than 90 days ago; no bridge letter provided

evidence.excerpt: Report period ended 2026-03-31; 213 days before 2026-10-30.

findings.deal_impact: Report period ended 2026-03-31, 213 days before the assessment date; controls may have changed since.

remediation.summary: Obtain a bridge letter covering through 2026-10-30.

findings.title: Critical subservice organization carved out of SOC 2 scope

evidence.excerpt: Nimbus Cloud Services is carved out of scope: infrastructure hosting.

findings.deal_impact: Nimbus Cloud Services (infrastructure hosting) is carved out of scope and is critical to production or in-scope data.

remediation.summary: Obtain the Nimbus Cloud Services SOC report and assess carve-out risk.

exceptions.description: MFA is enforced for all administrative access to production systems.
exceptions.management_response: Management disabled the legacy provisioning script in April 2026 and has begun migrating service-desk accounts to the standard conditional access policy. Migration expected to complete Q3 2026.

exceptions.description: Access for terminated employees is revoked within 1 business day of termination.
exceptions.management_response: Management is evaluating an automated HR-to-IdP de-provisioning integration. Until then, terminations are processed manually by IT upon email notification from HR.

exceptions.description: Security alerts generated by the SIEM are reviewed and triaged daily.
exceptions.management_response: The distribution list was corrected on November 24, 2025. Management has added a weekly check that alert routing is functioning.

exceptions.description: Production changes are approved by a peer before deployment.
exceptions.management_response: Management has updated the emergency change procedure to require post-deployment approval within 48 hours.

subservice_orgs.name: LedgerPay Payroll
subservice_orgs.services: HR and payroll processing, including employee termination records

cuecs: User entities are responsible for provisioning and de-provisioning their own users' access to the Brightwater platform.
User entities are responsible for enabling SSO/MFA for their users through the customer administration console.
User entities are responsible for reviewing user access to the platform at least quarterly.
User entities are responsible for notifying Brightwater promptly of suspected security incidents involving their accounts.
User entities are responsible for securing API credentials issued to them.
